title: How to Plan Your Rwanda Gorilla Trekking Permit
excerpt: Gorilla trekking in Rwanda is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Here's how to plan your permit, prepare for the trek and get the most out of your morning with the mountain gorillas.
content:
Few wildlife experiences compare to coming face to face with a mountain gorilla family in Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park. Spread across the mist-covered Virunga massif, the park is home to a population of mountain gorillas and a handful of habituated families that visitors can trek.

A gorilla permit is required for every trekker and is the single most important part of your planning. Permits are limited and issued for a specific date, so they are best secured early through your tour operator. Your permit includes park entry, the guided trek and one hour with your assigned gorilla family.

The trek begins early in the morning at the park headquarters near Kinigi. After a briefing, you are split into small groups and each group is assigned a gorilla family. Depending on where the family slept the previous night, the walk can be as short as thirty minutes or last several hours, sometimes up steep, muddy and forested slopes.

Wear sturdy hiking boots, long trousers, a rain jacket and gardening gloves, and carry drinking water on the trail. A porter can be hired at the start of the trek to help carry your bag and steady you on steep sections. Photography is allowed, but flash is not, and you should keep a respectful distance from the gorillas at all times.

The one hour you spend with the family passes quickly. Observing the silverback, the mothers and their playful infants in their natural forest home is an experience that stays with you long after you return to Kigali. Most travellers combine the trek with chimpanzee tracking, game drives and cultural visits across the country.

title: The Ultimate 7-Day Rwanda Safari Itinerary
excerpt: Seven days is enough time to see the best of Rwanda — gorillas in the Virungas, wildlife on the plains of Akagera, rainforest in Nyungwe and the shores of Lake Kivu. Here is a sample itinerary.
content:
Rwanda is small, well connected and remarkably easy to travel. In seven days you can cover the country's headline experiences without feeling rushed: gorilla trekking, a classic game drive, a rainforest canopy walk and a lakeside retreat.

Day one begins in Kigali. Arrive, settle in and, if energy allows, take a short guided city tour that covers the craft markets, hilltop viewpoints and a memorable introduction to Rwandan cuisine. Overnight in Kigali.

On day two, travel north to Volcanoes National Park. The drive through Rwanda's terraced green hills is a highlight in itself. Your afternoon is free to explore the surrounding villages, visit the historic sites in the area or simply rest ahead of your trek. Days three and four continue with your unforgettable encounter with the mountain gorillas.

From the volcanoes, travel south to Nyungwe National Park, one of Africa's oldest rainforests. Spend time on the canopy walk, spot monkeys and chimpanzees, and take an easy forest trail under the guidance of an experienced ranger.

Next, head towards the shores of Lake Kivu, where the pace slows. Enjoy a boat trip to the nearby islands and beaches, cycle a stretch of the Congo Nile Trail, or simply watch the sun set over the water from a lakeside terrace.

Finish with a relaxed drive back to Kigali or, if time allows, an optional day in Akagera National Park chasing the Big Five on a boat and game drive. Whatever you choose, your Global Line Safaris team will tailor the pace, accommodation and activities to your interests and travel style.
author: Alexis Rugamba

title: Akagera National Park: Rwanda's Big Five Safari Destination
excerpt: East, across the savannah plains of eastern Rwanda, Akagera National Park offers classic Big Five safaris on land and water — a wild side of Rwanda few expect.
content:
Most visitors think of Rwanda as a land of mountains and lakes, but eastern Rwanda hides a classic savannah wilderness. Akagera National Park covers more than a thousand square kilometres of open plains, acacia woodland and papyrus-fringed lakes along the border with Tanzania.

The park is home to lions, leopards, elephants, buffalo and rhinos, as well as giraffes, zebras and more than five hundred bird species. In recent years the reintroduction of lions and eastern black rhinos has restored Akagera to full Big Five status.

A day in Akagera typically starts with a morning game drive. Your guides know where the resident prides and elephant herds have been seen in the past days, giving you the best chance of quality sightings. The park's network of graded tracks makes it accessible in a comfortable safari vehicle.

The afternoon is a chance to take to the water. A boat trip on Lake Ihema drifts past pods of hippos, basking crocodiles and a remarkable variety of water birds, from fish eagles to herons and kingfishers. Sunset over the lake is one of the park's quiet highlights.

Akagera is easily reached from Kigali on a long day trip, but overnighting at the park makes the experience far richer. Watch for game at dusk from your lodge and return for an early morning drive before the heat of the day. title: Discovering Nyungwe Forest: Chimpanzees, Canopy Walk & Rainforest Trails
excerpt: In the south-west of Rwanda lies one of Africa's oldest rainforests. Nyungwe is a place of chimpanzees, canopy bridges and misty morning trails.
content:
Nyungwe National Park protects a vast tract of ancient montane rainforest in Rwanda's south-west. Scientists consider the forest among the oldest in Africa, and its altitude and rainfall have created a remarkable habitat: more than a thousand plant species and a dozen primate species, including large troops of chimpanzees.

Most visitors come for two experiences. The first is primate tracking. Rangers use moving listening posts to locate troops of chimpanzees as they feed in the fruiting trees, and the guided walks are a highlight of any Rwanda journey. Angolan colobus monkeys, in some of the largest troops on the continent, are also commonly seen along the trails.

The second is the canopy walk. A suspended bridge weaves high above the forest floor, offering unforgettable views over the undulating treetops and, on clear days, towards the mountains of the Albertine Rift. The walk is short, easy and suitable for most ages, and it is a wonderful way to watch the forest from the birds' perspective.

Nyungwe rewards those who slow down. The network of forest trails leads to waterfalls, swamps of giant lobelias, and quiet viewpoints far from any road. Early mornings are best, when the mist still clings to the canopy and the forest is most alive with birdsong.

Plan at least one full day for Nyungwe, or two if you want to combine chimpanzee tracking with the canopy walk and a longer trail. Global Line Safaris arranges park permits, lodging and a skilled local guide to make your rainforest visit smooth, safe and rewarding.

title: A Weekend Getaway at Lake Kivu: Villages, Beaches and the Congo Nile Trail
excerpt: Rwanda's largest lake is a place to slow down — coffee villages, quiet beaches, island boat trips and one of Africa's great lakeside walking routes.
content:
Lake Kivu stretches across the west of Rwanda, its deep blue waters framed by terraced hills and, on the far shore, the high peaks of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It is Rwanda's natural weekend retreat and a favourite way to end a safari.

The lake's resort towns each have a different character. Gisenyi in the north is lively and lakefront, with easy access to the volcanic region. Kibuye in the heart of the lake is quieter and arguably the most beautiful, with dramatic peninsulas, islands and sunsets. Karongi and Rubavu offer a range of lakeside lodges to suit every budget.

A boat trip is essential. Small wooden boats and organised excursions take you to the islands and beaches, including visits to fishermen's communities and, from Kibuye, Napoleon Island with its colony of fruit bats. Swimming is a pleasure in the deep, clear water.

For active travellers, the Congo Nile Trail runs along the lakeshore between Gisenyi and Kibuye. The route can be walked over several days or cycled in one or two, passing coffee and banana fields, village markets and breathtaking viewpoints over the water. It is one of the most scenic multi-day routes in East Africa.

A weekend on the lake is the perfect counterpoint to gorilla trekking or a wildlife safari. Global Line Safaris can build Lake Kivu into any itinerary, arranging boat trips, guides from the Congo Nile Trail, and welcoming lodges with the best views.

title: Kigali City Tour: A Day of History, Culture and Cuisine
excerpt: Before heading to the volcanoes or the savannah, spend a day in Kigali. Rwanda's capital is clean, green and full of story — from memorials to markets to craft coffee.
content:
Kigali is often the first and last stop on a Rwanda itinerary, and it deserves more than a single night. The city's hills carry a calm, progressive energy, and a day here fits in perfectly at the start or end of a safari.

Begin with the story of the city and the country at the Kigali Genocide Memorial, a place of remembrance that explains Rwanda's recent history with honesty and dignity. Visitors are asked to allow at least two hours and to approach the visit with respect. The memorial is widely regarded as essential to understanding modern Rwanda.

From there, the day turns to the livelier side of Kigali. The Kimironko market is a swirl of colour and bargain, where vendors sell fresh produce, fabrics and crafts. Nearby, the craft cooperative villages and local galleries showcase Rwandan art, weaving and souvenirs.

Food is a highlight. Rwanda's coffee is world class, and Kigali's speciality cafes serve it beautifully alongside local dishes. For lunch, try one of the city's restaurants offering home-style cuisine, including isombe, brochettes and fresh fish.

Finish with a drive to one of Kigali's viewpoint hills. From Mount Kigali or the hilltop viewpoints, the city unfolds below you in every shade of green. It is a fitting, peaceful close to a day in Rwanda's remarkable capital.
